description: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of problems based on correctness, categorized by whether knowledge was utilized and the type of error made, across difficulty levels of easy, medium, and hard. Each of the three charts contains four slices representing different error categories: “N+K+”, “N−K+”, “N−K−”, and “N+K−”. The “easy” chart shows slices of light green (40.6%), light orange (45.9%), light yellow (10.1%), and coral (3.3%). The “medium” chart displays slices of light green (44.6%), light orange (44.3%), light yellow (7.2%), and coral (3.9%). The “hard” chart includes slices of light green (36.2%), light orange (36.8%), light yellow (20.1%), and coral (7.0%). Each slice within the charts is labeled with its category and a percentage value. The charts include a legend identifying the categories, and the slices appear to be ordered clockwise from largest to smallest proportion within each chart.
caption_used: Problem distribution based on correctness under the w/ knowledge and w/o knowledge settings using CoT. The results indicate that while easier problems are primarily hindered by a lack of knowledge (N−K+ at approximately 50%), medium problems show a consistent dominance of reasoning-based errors (N−K− at 15%). For hard problems, the primary bottleneck lies in the inability to integrate geometric reasoning, as evidenced by the sharp decline in N+K+ to below 10%.
